mainTopic: Who carries the burden of proof when a giver may have been a שכיב מרע: רבה and רבי נתן's 'present condition' approach, its extension to doubts of טומאה, and the view of the חכמים
overview: This amud continues the case of a sick man who gave away his property and later died. Did he die from that same illness, so the gift stands, or did he recover first, which cancels it? רבה says his death proves he never recovered. אביי pushes back with a קל וחומר: with a sunken ship, where most people die, we still treat them as a doubt, so with sick people, who usually recover, we should doubt even more. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע shows that רבה follows רבי נתן in a ברייתא. There רבי יעקב leaves the property with the giver unless the recipients bring proof, while רבי נתן judges by the giver's present condition. רבי אלעזר says the same dispute applies to doubts of טומאה, using a משנה about a בקעה that is public for טומאה in summer and private in the rainy season. רבא limits that משנה: once a rainy season has passed over the field, it is private for both, which undercuts רבי אלעזר's comparison. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's next line, where the חכמים say that whoever takes from another must bring proof.

steps.title: רבה: His grave proves he died from that illness
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that since the giver is now dead, we assume he died from the same sickness and never recovered, so the gift stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Here he is dead, and his grave proves it about him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives his ruling on the dispute: the man is dead, and that fact itself shows he never got better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift from a שכיב מרע only stays valid if he dies from that illness. If he recovered, the gift falls away. רבה looks at the end result: the man died, so we assume the illness simply ran its course.

keyTerms.meaning: His grave proves it about him: his death shows what happened
A person who is deathly ill. His gifts follow special rules.
Here he is dead

phrases.english: Rabba said: Here he is dead,
and here his grave proves it about him.
phrases.notes: He means the man's death shows he never recovered from that sickness, so the gift stays.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַבָּה: הֲרֵי מֵת, וַהֲרֵי קִבְרוֹ מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the giver died, we assume he died of that illness without recovering, and the gift is valid.

steps.title: אביי: A sunken ship shows we should not assume this
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה with a קל וחומר. If we are unsure about people on a sunken ship, where most die, we should be even more unsure about sick people, since most of them recover.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Now think. With a ship that sank, where most people die, we still apply the stringencies of both the living and the dead to them. With sick people, where most recover, isn't that all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's ruling. He argues we cannot simply assume the sick man never recovered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a sunken ship, most passengers die, yet we still treat them as a doubt: maybe alive, maybe dead. Most sick people get better. So it makes even more sense that this man may have recovered before he died. That would cancel the gift.

keyTerms.meaning: A ship (here, one that sank)
The strict rules of the living and the strict rules of the dead, applied together because of a doubt
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
Majority; what usually happens

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Now, if with a ship, where most of them are lost,

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתְנִין עֲלֵיהֶן חוּמְרֵי חַיִּים וְחוּמְרֵי מֵתִים;
phrases.english: we apply to them the stringencies of the living and the stringencies of the dead;
sick people, where most sick people recover to life,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הַשְׁתָּא, וּמָה סְפִינָה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's assumption that the giver's death proves he never recovered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if we treat sunken-ship passengers as a doubt even though most die, we must surely treat a sick person as possibly recovered, since most sick people do recover.

steps.title: רבה's view follows רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע identifies רבה's ruling as matching the opinion of רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: Whose view does this teaching of רבה follow? It follows רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא steps in to tie רבה's ruling to a תנא. He says it matches רבי נתן. He is setting up the ברייתא he will quote next as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רבה is not inventing a new idea. His ruling rests on one side of an older dispute among תנאים, so it stands even after אביי's challenge if one follows רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does it follow?
A teaching or ruling

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
In accordance with whom does this teaching of Rabba go?
In accordance with Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places רבה's ruling inside an earlier dispute among תנאים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה's ruling matches the view of רבי נתן.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יעקב puts the burden on the recipients
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks who must prove what when a giver claims he was sick and can take back his gift. רבי יעקב says the giver keeps the property without proof, and the recipients need proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Who takes from whom? He takes from them without proof, but they cannot take from him except with proof. These are the words of רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that backs up step 3. This step gives the first opinion, רבי יעקב's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The property was originally the giver's. So רבי יעקב leaves it with him, and the recipients must prove he was healthy when he gave it. He does not look at the giver's present condition at all.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Takes property out of someone's possession
Proof

phrases.english: As it was taught:
Who takes out of whose possession?
phrases.notes: The giver says he was sick, so he can take the gift back. The recipients say he was healthy.

phrases.english: He takes out of their possession without proof,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן אֵין מוֹצִיאִין מִיָּדוֹ אֶלָּא בִּרְאָיָה;
phrases.english: but they cannot take out of his possession except with proof;
these are the words of Rabbi Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source cited for step 3
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that רבה follows רבי נתן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute of רבי יעקב and רבי נתן

steps.title: רבי נתן: Judge by his present condition
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says we judge by how the giver is now. If he is healthy now, he must prove he was sick. If he is sick now, the recipients must prove he was healthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: If he is healthy, he must bring proof that he was deathly ill. If he is deathly ill, they must bring proof that he was healthy.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second opinion in the ברייתא. It is the one רבה's ruling matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן assumes a person's present condition shows what his condition was before. רבה uses the same kind of thinking: the man is dead now, so we assume he was dying all along. Whoever claims a change must bring proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Healthy
The burden of proof is on him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יעקב: the property stays with the giver unless the recipients prove otherwise. רבי נתן: go by his present condition. Whoever claims it was different must prove it. רבה follows רבי נתן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
If he is healthy,
phrases.notes: He means healthy now, at the time of the court case.

phrases.aramaic: עָלָיו לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה שֶׁהָיָה שְׁכִיב מְרַע.
phrases.english: it is upon him to bring proof that he was deathly ill.
If he is deathly ill,
it is upon them to bring proof that he was healthy.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: אִם בָּרִיא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבה's assumption that the present state (death) shows the earlier state (dying)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן's rule that the burden of proof follows the giver's present condition

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: The same dispute applies to impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that questions of טומאה also depend on this dispute. He begins quoting a משנה about a field (בקעה) that counts differently for שבת and for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: And for טומאה, it is like the dispute. As we learned: A בקעה in the summer is a רשות היחיד for שבת, and a רשות הרבים for טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר widens the dispute to cases of doubtful טומאה. He starts quoting the משנה that shows it, and the next step finishes the quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doubt about טומאה in a רשות הרבים is ruled pure, but in a רשות היחיד it is ruled impure. A בקעה in summer has many people passing through, so for טומאה it counts as public. The rest of the משנה will show how the ruling can depend on the present season, which links to רבי נתן's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity
Like the dispute: it depends on the same disagreement
An open expanse of fields
Private domain
Public domain

steps.confusionAlert: The same field can be a רשות היחיד for שבת and a רשות הרבים for טומאה. Each area of law defines 'public' in its own way, so these do not contradict each other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
And for impurity, it is like the dispute.
phrases.notes: He means the dispute between רבי יעקב and רבי נתן we just saw.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
An expanse of fields in the summer days
is a private domain for Shabbat,
and a public domain for impurity.
phrases.notes: For a doubt about טומאה in a public area, we rule the person or item pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the רבי יעקב / רבי נתן dispute to the laws of טומאה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doubtful cases of טומאה depend on the same dispute as the gift of a שכיב מרע. The proof from the משנה about a בקעה is completed in the next step.

steps.title: In the rainy season the field is a private domain for both
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר finishes quoting the משנה: in the rainy season, an open field counts as a private domain both for שבת and for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the rainy season, the field is a private domain both for this (שבת) and for that (טומאה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the משנה that רבי אלעזר began quoting in the last step. In the rainy season, the field counts as a private domain for both שבת and טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the summer the field is a private domain for שבת but a public domain for טומאה. In the rainy season few people walk there, so it is a private domain for both, and a doubt of טומאה there makes a person טמא. So if a person does not know which season he entered, רבי יעקב says he keeps his earlier status (טהור), and רבי נתן says we judge by the season he is asking in, just like in the gift case.

keyTerms.meaning: The rainy season (winter)
Private domain
For this and for that, meaning for both שבת and טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of 'private domain.' For שבת it is about carrying. For טומאה it matters because a doubt of טומאה in a private domain makes a person טמא, but in a public domain he stays טהור.

phrases.english: In the rainy season,
phrases.notes: This finishes the משנה about the field that רבי אלעזר started quoting in the step before.

phrases.english: it is a private domain for this and for that.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means for שבת and for טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לְכָאן וּלְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted by רבי אלעזר in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the rainy season, an open field is a private domain for both שבת and טומאה, so the season matters when there is a doubt of טומאה. That is where the dispute of רבי יעקב and רבי נתן would come in.

steps.title: רבא limits the field rule to before the rainy season passes
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה's rule only applies if a rainy season has not yet passed over the field. If it has, the field is a private domain for both, so there is no parallel dispute about טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They only taught this when the rainy season had not passed over the field. But if the rainy season had passed over it, it is a private domain for this and for that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with רבי אלעזר by limiting when the משנה's rule applies. Once a rainy season has passed over the field, it is a private domain for both, all year round.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule that the field is public for טומאה in the summer applies only if no rainy season has passed since the doubt came up. If one has passed, the field stays a private domain for טומאה even in the summer, so the person is טמא even according to רבי נתן. That removes the parallel that רבי אלעזר tried to draw to the gift dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when... (a phrase that limits a ruling)
Passed over it (time went by over the field)
An אמורא who here limits the משנה's rule

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the dispute between רבי יעקב and רבי נתן does not automatically carry over to doubts of טומאה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They only taught this
where the rainy season had not passed over it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the field. He means no rainy season has gone by since the doubt of טומאה came up.

phrases.english: but if the rainy season had passed over it,
it is a private domain for this and for that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה that רבי אלעזר used, which undercuts his comparison.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אלעזר's claim that doubts of טומאה in the field also depend on the רבי יעקב and רבי נתן dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Once a rainy season has passed, the field is a private domain for טומאה all year. So the person is טמא no matter which season he asks in, and there is nothing to argue about.

steps.title: The חכמים: the one taking from another must bring proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the חכמים say the one who wants to take property from someone else must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: The one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves on to the next line of the משנה, the opinion of the חכמים. This line sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים use the general rule that whoever wants to take property out of someone else's hands must prove his claim. Here the property is still with the giver, so the recipients are the ones taking from him, and they must bring proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who wants to take from his fellow must bring proof
The Sages, the majority opinion in the משנה
And so on: the rest of the quote is left out

steps.whatToRemember: The basic rule of the חכמים: whoever wants to take property from someone else carries the burden of proof. Here that means the recipients.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
The one who takes from his fellow, the proof is upon him, etc.
phrases.notes: The property is still with the giver, so the recipients are the ones 'taking' and must prove their claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the טומאה discussion and quotes the next line of the משנה to start a new discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the burden of proof is on the one who wants to take property from another. Here that is the recipients.
